cards.b: Breathing feels automatic, yet it is the link between the air and every cell's energy factory. The lungs bring oxygen in and carbon dioxide out. India's air pollution and TB make this system a major public health topic.

Air enters the nose (warmed, filtered), passes the pharynx, larynx (voice box) and trachea (windpipe, held open by cartilage rings), then branches into two bronchi, many bronchioles and ends in tiny sacs called alveoli.

cards.h: How we breathe in and out
cards.b:
Breathing is driven by pressure.

  1. Inhale: the diaphragm flattens and ribs rise, so the chest grows. Pressure drops and air rushes in.
  2. Exhale: muscles relax, the chest shrinks, and air is pushed out.

The medulla in the brain controls rate, mostly triggered by rising CO2, not low oxygen.

About 300-500 million alveoli give a surface of roughly 70 square metres. Their walls and neighbouring capillaries are one cell thick. Oxygen moves into blood and carbon dioxide moves out by simple diffusion, driven by differences in partial pressure.

About 97 percent of oxygen rides on haemoglobin in red cells. Carbon dioxide travels mostly as bicarbonate in plasma, with some on haemoglobin and some dissolved. Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin about 200 times more strongly than oxygen, which is why it is so dangerous.
A normal breath moves about 500 ml (tidal volume). Total lung capacity is roughly 5-6 litres, and vital capacity (largest breath out) about 3.5-4.5 litres. A spirometer measures these.
Lavoisier (1780s) linked breathing to burning. Christian Bohr (1904) showed CO2 helps haemoglobin release oxygen (Bohr effect). Smoking's link to lung cancer was shown by Doll and Hill in 1950.

Fix these

  • Lungs do not have muscles; the diaphragm and rib muscles do the work.
  • Exhaled air still has about 16 percent oxygen, which makes mouth-to-mouth rescue possible.
  • The urge to breathe comes from CO2 rise.

India has the largest TB burden in the world; the national goal is to end TB by 2025, later extended, under the National TB Elimination Programme. Many Indian cities have high PM2.5 levels, tied to asthma and COPD. The National Clean Air Programme (2019) targets cuts in particle levels. Indian yogic breathing (pranayama) has been studied for effects on lung function.

• Air path: nose, trachea, bronchi, alveoli.
  • The diaphragm creates pressure change.
  • Exchange by diffusion in alveoli.
  • Haemoglobin carries oxygen; CO binds too tightly.

Think about it:

  1. Why are alveoli so numerous and thin?
  2. Why does holding breath become unbearable?
